text: In 1954, French rule in Indochina is coming apart.
In a valley near Laos, Viet Minh guns ring a French base at Dien Bien Phu. After eight weeks of siege, the garrison falls on 7 May.
At Geneva, Vietnam is divided along the 17th parallel. The North goes to Ho Chi Minh, the South to a French-backed state.
In Saigon, Ngo Dinh Diem declares a republic and takes power.
From 1959, the North sends men and weapons south along trails through Laos.
At Ap Bac, in the Mekong Delta, a guerrilla battalion beats a much larger southern force. Five American helicopters are lost.
In August 1964, American destroyers report attacks in the Gulf of Tonkin. Congress gives the president a free hand.
In March 1965, Marines come ashore at Da Nang. They are the first American combat troops in Vietnam.
In November, the Ia Drang valley sees the first large battle between American and North Vietnamese units.
By the end of 1965, nearly two hundred thousand American troops are in the country. And the war is only beginning.
